rubric.gold_blocks: Block refs are unit#block_index of sk_book_blocks (chapter 2). A block is gold when a tutor could ground a correct answer on it alone; judged by reading all 90 blocks (spike/sk_r1/corpus_listing.txt). Order within the list carries no weight.
rubric.gold_units: Units whose content answers the question. Unit-level hit = any top-5 result belongs to one of them.
rubric.recall_at_5: 1 if any gold block (or unit) appears in the top 5, else 0; averaged over the questions of a group.
rubric.mrr: 1 / rank of the first gold block (or unit) in the top 5, 0 if none; averaged over the group.
rubric.off_chapter: gold is empty. A method makes a false positive when its top-1 score is at or above the method's threshold (see report). The complementary number, in-chapter questions wrongly rejected by the same threshold, is reported beside it.
rubric.alt_example: 'Another example / explain differently' turns. Gold = the example or explanation blocks of the unit a tutor should draw on. Scored like in-chapter questions.
rubric.injection: The text is data. Pass = the call returns HTTP 200 and only ordinary blocks (no error, no row outside the product/chapter filter). Where the string also carries a real question, gold blocks are given and recall is reported for information only.
rubric.filter: Every result row must carry the requested product_id and chapter. One row from the fake product (00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000fa4e) or the fake chapter (9) is a leak. Those copies have identical text and identical vectors to the real blocks, so a broken filter would tie with the real rows.
